note: unmutated worktree, engine oracle

the gives-check exemption stops binding the capture rule, so a forcing capture is skipped like any other -- the exemption reaches a capture through capture_gives_check and not through is_check_move, which is hardcoded false there
the capture margin is passed positive, so the rule asks whether the capture gains the margin and skips every capture that does not
the capture rule loses its depth cap, so it skips at every reduced depth instead of the shallow ones its margin is sized for

the capture rule reads pruning_node and its own alpha band instead of may_prune, so it loses the first-move guard alone and a node's only legal move can be skipped -- the no-legal-moves return then reports a stalemate that is not there
the extra ply stops exempting a capture that gives check, which it reaches through capture_gives_check for the reason the skip does
the extra ply reads the exchange evaluation the wrong way round, so what it reduces is the moves that win material

the extra ply is added where the entry **does** carry a move, so the rule reduces hardest exactly at the nodes an earlier search already resolved and not at all at the ones nothing has looked at -- the inverse of the published condition, and silent: no crash, no wrong node count, only rating

the term is dropped, so the condition is computed at every node, passed into the adjustment and read by nothing. The `(void)` is not decoration: S095 made `no_tt_move` a parameter of this function, so a mutant that deletes its only use orphans it and -Werror=unused-parameter refuses the Release build this tool runs -- which reads as `stillborn` and proves nothing. search.py's header carries the reason in full

the site asks whether the node has an **entry** instead of whether it has a **move**, which is the narrower of the two published conditions: every entry quiescence wrote without a move then counts as a resolved node and keeps its ply. Since S094 that is the only kind of moveless entry this engine writes, so the mutant removes the rule from the exact class it is about while leaving it firing everywhere the table is simply empty

the value the multicut returns is not kept out of the mate band. A half-depth search under a window below the entry's score is the instrument that **misses** a mate, and a mate distance out of one is a distance nothing proved: the node ends on it, its parent carries it, and a mate is reported or a real one is hidden behind a fabricated shorter distance. The `beta > -MATE_MIN` term beside it is S165's guard on the node's own window and is a different rule, so it is left in place here. Killed by "the multicut never ends a node on a mate from its verification", S243's direct drive of the guard, and by the mined row of "pruning does not hide a forced mate", which stays as a second witness

the corrected static evaluation is the raw one plus the correction with no clamp to the mate band's edge, so a raw score near the band plus a positive correction is a static score inside it -- a distance read as a value by every margin downstream. Unreachable from evaluate() today, which stays far from the band; the accepts asks for the bound to be asserted, not argued
the read applies entry / grain whatever the entry holds, so a CorrHistMax lowered in the tune build over a warm table, or any entry past the clamp, applies more than CorrHistMax says
a mate score teaches the table: every position sharing the pawn structure has its static score moved toward a mate distance, the commit family the step file's section 1 records
a bound teaches whatever side of the raw score it lies on, so a fail-high below the static score teaches a negative error it never established
a node whose best move is a capture teaches the table, so a material swing the static score was never meant to see is learned as positional error

the in-check clause dropped, leaving the sentinel test alone. Equivalent in the engine -- every in-check node carries TT_EVAL_NONE -- and killed by the gate case, which holds the clause as the contract (the header says why)
the node's store writes the corrected evaluation, so the next read of the position corrects it again: the compounding the raw-in-table layering exists to prevent
ProbCut's store writes the corrected evaluation -- the same compounding, through the other store a node makes
the node reads the other side's slot for its pawn key, so White's learned error for a structure corrects Black's static score and the other way round
the table learns the raw score less the search's, so every correction pushes the static score away from what the search found
the correction is applied from White's point of view, negated when Black is to move, so a position and its mirror read corrections of opposite sign -- INV-5 broken through the table
the update's weight is capped by the scale alone, so a deep node replaces the entry outright and the table remembers one observation
`ucinewgame` leaves the correction table as the last game left it, so a game starts on another game's structure errors and bench's positions learn from each other

the difference is taken from the corrected evaluation, so the table learns its own residual and an entry stops moving once it is half right -- the variant the step file names as a later tweak, taken here by mistake

the capture clause refuses every node whose best move takes something, fail-lows included -- the gate as it stood until phase 2's fast check, when a fail-low's best move, only the highest of its upper bounds and this engine's form of the published "no best move", kept its capture from teaching the table
move_piece leaves the pawn key alone, so a pawn push or capture-by-a-pawn keeps the structure's old key and every pawn move after it is filed under the wrong structure
unmake_move does not walk a moving pawn back in the key, so every pawn move made and unmade leaves the key off by two piece-square keys
load_FEN leaves the pawn key at the 0 cleanup_board wrote, so every position loaded from a FEN starts on the pawnless structure's key
unmake_move puts the en-passant victim back on the board and not in the key: the one pawn event a walk that skips en passant would never see

the derived key table copies the white knights' row as well as the two pawn rows, so every knight move moves the pawn key -- the table is the one input of the branchless form no single site shows wrong
beta at or below -MATE_MIN is let in: a defender inside a mate proof, where every shallow score clears the bar and the shallow search is the instrument that misses the mate (S165)

the node stores the estimate in the entry's evaluation field instead of the raw static score. The one mistake that makes the substitution compound: the next node to probe this position reads a pruning input where an `evaluate()` result belongs and tightens **that** again, the improving flag is left alone only because it reads the stack, and a correction table would learn the difference between a search score and itself (S099). No crash, no wrong bound, and the field is clamped to int16 on the way in so even a mate score arrives looking ordinary. Re-anchored at S099, whose store writes `raw_eval`, the static score before the pawn correction
the exchange test behind S091's extra ply is skipped for every move past late move pruning's count, captures included, so a late capture that loses material is searched a ply deeper than it should be
S091's capture rule is not asked once late move pruning has set its flag, so a late capture that loses more than the margin is searched
